data.name: Devendrasinh
data.long_meaning: Devendra means the lord of gods and Sinh means lion. So, Devendrasinh means the god who is the lord of all gods and has the strength of a lion.
data.spiritual_meaning: Devendrasinh is a powerful name that signifies the divine presence of the almighty God within a person. It is believed that a person with this name is blessed with immense courage and strength, and is protected by the gods.
data.numerology_meaning: Devendrasinh is a name with a strong vibration that represents power, authority, and leadership. The name resonates with the energy of the Universal Spirit and is a reminder of the divine connection that exists within each of us.

data.cultural_impact: Devendrasinh is a revered name in Hindu culture, representing divine power and royalty. Devendra, as the lord of gods, signifies the supreme being and the ruler of the cosmos. The incorporation of the lion (Sinh) adds to the name's significance as a symbol of courage, power, and sovereignty. This name would have been particularly esteemed in ancient Hindu societies where mythology and puranic tales centered on gods, their attributes, and their divine realms.
data.spiritual_significance: Devendrasinh carries a supreme and divine connotation, emphasizing the connection between the individual and the divine. A person named Devendrasinh could be seen as a representation of the devotee's deep-rooted faith, expressing their belief in the supreme power of God as Protector, Sustainer, and Dissolver of all. This spiritual significance also highlights the inner strength and courage required to live life with reverence to the divine. The name, therefore, serves as a constant reminder of this sacred connection and embodies the ultimate goal of one's spiritual journey.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Devendra is the name of a king mentioned in the Mahabharata. The name Devendrasinh carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an epic Sanskrit text, one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. It narrates the Kurukshetra war between the Pandava and the Kaurava princes and their allies.
